title: Coin change: step-by-step greedy selection
summary: At each step, pick the largest denomination not exceeding the remaining amount, reducing 131 down to 0.
context: The target amount is 131, and candidate denominations [1, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100] may each be used repeatedly. The callout states "Greedy strategy: always choose the largest coin that does not exceed the remaining amount".
description: From top to bottom, rows list remaining amounts 131, 31, 11, 1, and 0. Each of the first four rows displays the same candidate denominations with 100, 20, 10, and 1 highlighted in turn while unchosen coins are gray, linked across adjacent rows by dashed arrows. The final row reaches remaining amount 0 with no candidate row drawn.

Each row shows the balance after the previous coins have been subtracted. The highlighted coin is the next one to subtract. For example, 31 is the balance after subtracting 100. The highlighted 20 is deducted when the balance changes to 11. The table below lists coins already used, next coin chosen, and resulting balance at each row.

frames.title: Four greedy selections reduce remaining amount 131 to 0
frames.explanation: Four coins are used in total—100 + 20 + 10 + 1 = 131—leaving denominations 5 and 50 unused. For this denomination set 4 coins is also the global minimum, though for arbitrary denominations the greedy strategy does not always minimize coin count.

prose.title: Coin change: making 131
prose.summary: Five steps show the remaining balance before each of the four coin picks followed by the final zero balance.
context: Target amount is 131 with reusable denominations [1, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100]. Each step selects the largest denomination not exceeding the remaining balance.
description: In the first four steps, the highlighted coin is the upcoming pick and is subtracted only upon advancing to the next step. Gray means unchosen in the current step rather than permanently disabled. Step 5 reaches balance 0, hides the coin row, and stops.
prose.result: Here 4 coins achieve the minimum count; for other denomination sets, greedy selection is not guaranteed to be optimal.

steps.title: Remaining 131: select largest available coin 100 next
steps.explanation: Starting at balance 131 with 0 coins used so far, the largest candidate denomination not exceeding 131 is 100, so select 100 next (not yet subtracted); subtracting it reduces the next balance to 131 - 100 = 31.
steps.key_state: Remaining balance 131, used so far: none (0 coins), next pick: 100 (not yet subtracted).
steps.announcement: Initial balance 131: select largest available denomination 100, leaving 31 after subtraction.

steps.title: Remaining 31: 100 subtracted, select 20 next
steps.explanation: After subtracting 100, the remaining balance is 31 (1 coin used so far: 100). Denominations 50 and 100 exceed 31, so the largest valid denomination is 20; the highlighted 20 is selected next (not yet subtracted) and will reduce the balance to 31 - 20 = 11.
steps.key_state: Remaining balance 31, used so far: 1 coin (100), next pick: 20 (not yet subtracted).
steps.announcement: After subtracting 100, balance is 31; select 20 next, leaving 11 after subtraction.

steps.title: Remaining 11: two coins used, select 10 next
steps.explanation: After subtracting 20, the remaining balance is 11 (2 coins used so far: 100, 20, totaling 120). Denominations 20, 50, and 100 exceed 11, so the largest valid denomination is 10; select 10 next (not yet subtracted), which will reduce the balance to 11 - 10 = 1.
steps.key_state: Remaining balance 11, used so far: 2 coins (100, 20), next pick: 10 (not yet subtracted).
steps.announcement: After subtracting 20, balance is 11; select 10 next, leaving 1 after subtraction.

steps.title: Remaining 1: three coins used, select final coin 1
steps.explanation: After subtracting 10, the remaining balance is 1 (3 coins used so far: 100, 20, 10, totaling 130). Because 5, 10, 20, 50, and 100 all exceed 1, select smallest denomination 1 next (not yet subtracted), which will reduce the balance to 1 - 1 = 0.
steps.key_state: Remaining balance 1, used so far: 3 coins (100, 20, 10), next pick: 1 (not yet subtracted).
steps.announcement: After subtracting 10, balance is 1; select 1 next to reduce the balance to 0.

steps.title: Balance reduced to 0: four coins complete the target
steps.explanation: Subtracting the 4th coin, 1, reduces the remaining balance to 0, hides the candidate coin row, and ends selection. Across four steps, 4 coins—100, 20, 10, and 1—sum to 100 + 20 + 10 + 1 = 131, leaving denominations 5 and 50 unused.
steps.key_state: Remaining balance 0; 4 coins (100, 20, 10, 1) make 131, completing coin change.
steps.announcement: Subtracting 1 brings the balance to 0, completing 131 with 4 coins.
